title: Declared entry formats for the shared append-only artifacts
description: THE single declaration of where each shared append-only artifact's ENTRY FORMAT is defined. The population is NOT declared here: it is JOINED from pipeline-state-paths.json on transient:false, which invariant I95 already binds in both directions and which fails closed. This file declares only the OTHER side of that join -- for each durable name, the shipped file that states what one entry looks like, and the anchor inside it that a reader resolves. THE DUTY IS THAT A FORMAT EXISTS AND IS DECLARED, NOT THAT A WRITE SITE LOCATES ONE. A duty to LOCATE a format before writing was built first and refuted on measurement: it is discharged by looking, so a competently written locate-duty firing on nothing scores as a shipped fix, and a vacuous locate-duty and a real one are spelled identically. An existence-and-declaration duty has a subject a checker can address. Format steering was attached at 3 of 24 shared append-only artifacts and absent at 21 when this was filed, and which writes got it depended on which core author added a READ AND FOLLOW sentence at that call site rather than on any property of the write.

join.description: How the POPULATION is derived. Declared as data rather than hard-coded in the reader so the reader and this file cannot disagree about which artifacts are in scope. Hand-listing the population here would create a second copy of a set I95 already owns, and the two would drift in the direction that reads as clean.

population_schema.description: The schema that OWNS the population, resolved in both layouts (core/schemas/ in the distribution, .claude/schemas/ on a consumer).

population_key.description: The field inside each entry of that schema's `paths` array that selects membership.

population_value.description: The value of population_key that selects membership. false selects the DURABLE half -- the artifacts a consumer commits and later sessions append to, which is exactly the set where an undeclared entry format costs something.

formats.description: One entry per durable artifact whose format IS declared. The reader set-compares this against the joined population: a durable artifact with no entry here is reported, and an entry naming a name that is not in the population is reported too. Both directions, because a declaration for an artifact nothing writes is as wrong as an artifact nothing declares.

name.description: The top-level name under the pipeline root, spelled EXACTLY as pipeline-state-paths.json spells it. This string is the JOIN KEY, so any decoration -- a trailing slash, a root prefix -- makes the set-compare fail on a correctly declared artifact.

declared_in.description: A path, relative to the distribution root, to the shipped file that STATES the entry format. Checked for existence AND for containing the anchor, because a declaration pointing at a file that no longer carries the format is the failure this whole file exists to make visible.

anchor.description: A literal substring that must appear in declared_in. It is what makes this a binding rather than a filename: a whole-file check is satisfied by the artifact's name appearing anywhere, including in a comment, and that is how a format declaration goes stale without anything reporting it. The anchor is the format's own marker, region label or field name -- something that cannot survive the format being deleted.

kind.description: How the format is carried. `schema` is a core/schemas/*.json field or key block a program LOADS; `generated-region` is a BEGIN/END GENERATED region rendered from a schema; `prose` is a shipped rule or step file that states the entry shape in text. The tier is recorded because the three are not equally durable -- prose is the weakest and is the class that decayed here -- and because a later arm can raise the floor without re-deriving the population.

note.description: Optional. What is known about the declaration's limits. Present where the format is partial, so a reader does not take a declared entry as a promise of completeness.

formats.name: audit-anchors.md
formats.note: The strongest carrier in the set: the header is RENDERED by validate-audit-anchors.sh --render into a BEGIN/END GENERATED region and byte-compared, and every entry is validated against the schema's own `fields` map.

formats.name: gate-adjudication
formats.note: A verdict file under this directory is a standalone JSON document the validator json.loads; the envelope marker is the schema_id string.

formats.name: ai-dlc-update
formats.note: Declares the register at ai-dlc-update/layer-adjudication-register.jsonl. The pull LEDGERS that share this directory are not covered by it.

formats.name: implementation-artifacts
formats.note: Declares sprint-status.yaml under this directory. gate-log.md and gate-metrics.jsonl, which sit beside it, carry their own entries here.

formats.name: party-mode-transcripts
formats.note: The provenance block a transcript carries is rendered from this schema into retro.md's generated region and byte-matched by validate-retro-evidence.sh. The transcript BODY has no declared shape.
